newsitem.title: USA: Mass. expects to issue about $22 mln UPLAN bonds.
newsitem.headline: Mass. expects to issue about $22 mln UPLAN bonds.

text.p: Massachusetts expects to issue about $22 million of special obligation bonds later this Spring to finance its UPLAN program, the state's educational financing agency said on Monday.

Since the program's 1995 inception, some 33,400 participants from 33 states and nine countries, have invested in approximately $45 million of the bonds that form the basis for a prepaid tuition savings program.

The program allows investors to lock-in the cost of future tuition at current rates at 83 participating colleges in the state, including Boston College, Smith College, Wellesley College as well as University of Massachusetts.

"The great thing about the UPLAN is that it helps thousands of Massachusetts families keep pace with the rising cost of college without putting the taxpayer on the hook," said Massachusetts Treasurer Joe Malone whose office issues the special general obligation bonds.
Peter Mazareas, executive director of the Massachusetts Educational Financing Authority, which administers the program, explained the bonds are offered with maturities between five and 20 years.

He said that a General Accounting Office study found that between 1981 and 1995, the cost of tuition at public universities rose by 234 percent, but that real wages only grew by 82 percent for the same time period.
"UPLAN represents a tremendous return for the investor. Not only do they lock in today's tuition, but they also get a tax break," said Mazareas.
